worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2. After subtracting the proposal cost of 6, continued support yields −4. The coalition therefore decided not to support the federal proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that withdrawals of support will be preceded by internal documents discussing deterioration in competitive benefits, rather than changes in expected alternative-regulation burdens.
worlds.derivation: Under CA, support responds to incremental competitive benefit net of proposal cost. A benefit reduction to 2 makes the payoff negative, whereas a change only in alternative-regulation burden does not affect the CA payoff.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can identify and temporally order relevant internal documents.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice lowered the expected burden from alternative carbon regulation from 12 to 2. The incremental competitive benefit remains 12, so subtracting the proposal cost of 6 leaves a payoff of 6. The coalition decided to continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to endorse the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict continued-support records even after internal assessments sharply reduce the expected burden of alternative regulation, provided competitive-benefit assessments remain favorable.
worlds.derivation: CA makes the support payoff depend on competitive benefit minus proposal cost. The reduced regulatory burden is therefore behaviorally irrelevant when competitive benefit remains 12 and the cost is 6.
worlds.extra_assumption: Document retention does not systematically exclude assessments of alternative regulation.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice revised the expected burden of alternative regulation downward to 2 but left the incremental competitive benefit at 12. Net of the proposal cost of 6, the relevant payoff is 6. The coalition decided to maintain support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition maintains its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: In a larger documentary sample, revisions to support should correlate more strongly with revised competitive-benefit estimates than with revised estimates of alternative-regulation burdens.
worlds.derivation: The CA decision rule uses competitive benefit net of proposal cost, while alternative-regulation burden does not enter the payoff. Decision and communication errors add noise but are independent.
worlds.extra_assumption: The documentary sample contains enough comparable proposals to estimate associations.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private commercial assessment cut the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2. With the common proposal cost of 6 deducted once, continued support has a payoff of −4. The coalition decided to withdraw support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict occasional contradictions between internal decision records and subsequent public statements, without corresponding evidence that the underlying commercial assessment changed overnight.
worlds.derivation: The memo records the actual decision faithfully, while the public note independently reports the opposite decision with probability .05. Thus documentary contradiction can arise from communication error rather than a new payoff calculation.
worlds.extra_assumption: No intervening decision occurs between the internal memo and public note.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice reduced the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2. Competitive benefit remains 12. After subtracting the proposal cost of 6, continued support yields 6, and the coalition decided to keep supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition remains in support of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal memoranda sustaining endorsement will explicitly preserve a positive competitive rationale even when they acknowledge weaker regulatory pressure.
worlds.derivation: Under CA, weaker alternative-regulation pressure does not alter the payoff; continued support follows because the unchanged competitive benefit exceeds the proposal cost.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal authors normally record the considerations they regard as decision-relevant.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice lowered the expected burden associated with alternative carbon regulation to 2 while leaving the incremental competitive benefit at 12. The relevant net payoff remains 6 after the proposal cost. The coalition decided to continue its endorsement.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to endorse the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: When internal documents distinguish regulatory exposure from competitive advantage, researchers should predict that endorsements persist specifically in cases where only regulatory-exposure estimates deteriorate.
worlds.derivation: CA excludes alternative-regulation burden from the support payoff and retains support when competitive benefit of 12 exceeds cost of 6, apart from rare decision reversals.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can distinguish the two benefit categories reliably from document language.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private notice reduced the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2 but did not alter the incremental competitive benefit of 12. Net benefit from continued support is therefore 6 after the proposal cost. The coalition decided to maintain support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal discussions of continued support emphasize competitive positioning even where contemporaneous files report declining concern about alternative regulation.
worlds.derivation: The CA mechanism makes competitive benefit decisive and leaves alternative-regulation burden outside the payoff calculation; the generated configuration illustrates how the two assessments can diverge.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal discussions provide enough substantive reasoning to identify emphasis.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice cut the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2, producing a payoff of −4 after subtracting the proposal cost of 6. Despite that result, the coalition reversed the prescribed choice and decided to continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict a small minority of internal decisions that conflict with the recorded payoff calculation, appearing as isolated reversals rather than systematic responses to a particular notice category.
worlds.derivation: A negative CA payoff ordinarily implies withdrawal, but the decision is independently reversed with probability .05. Independence implies that such anomalies should not systematically track notice content beyond the underlying prescribed decision.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal records document both the payoff assessment and the final decision.
